base: main ab1a361e8; measured on a private copy of 535538242 (research/substrate-ab/m1/copy.sh) running main's SDK vdd8ppwp and checkout platform k3f6kmfx, so its VM was its own
command: bl test test/bl/scene/frame_plan_test.bl, after `realm stop` (warm) or as `bin/bl --cold` (cold); the m1.py first-in-fresh-vm/test and cold/test rows
how: research/substrate-ab/m3/drive.py: pairs of (realm stop; first command through the warm path) and (realm stop; --cold), wall from the driver. Traced runs load research/substrate-ab/m3/m3_trace.erl at VM boot (ERL_AFLAGS=-s m3_trace start): call/return of ~25 named functions (session start, listen, request handler, manager start, realm open, handle-in-vm, dev-overlay sync, loader ensure_loaded/do_load/compile_sdk_source!, retain_sdk_runtime!, sdk_runtime_inventory_uncached!), every call >= 20 ms written with its wall-clock start, so VM phases line up with the driver's t0. phases_ms_median_n5.note: tr2 + tr3, 5 warm and 5 cold traced runs; each warm row is extra work the cold path does not do, except where marked

findings.card_premise: The client's readiness wait is not where the time goes. The VM listens before its services start; the client's 200 ms hello poll plus the reconnect took 40-296 ms (median 171), and the request then waited inside the VM for the boot's services, which finished 472-792 ms (median 626) after the request arrived. So sending the request at once (this branch's client) only moves the wait inside the VM.
findings.global_lock_backoff: The boot and the first request take the same locks: vm.manager/start (:vm-manager-start, batch 25's dupstart fix), the realm lifecycle, the session live table, and the loader's per-file :bl_load locks. All are :global.trans or :global.set_lock with infinite retries, whose sleep after a failed attempt is uniform in 0-250 ms, then 0-500 ms, 0-1 s and up to 8 s (kernel-11.0.1 global.erl random_sleep). In tr2 warm 2 the request's manager start ended 285 ms after the boot released the lock. trans_check.bl, same workload (holder 300 ms, waiter 20 ms in): :global.trans waiter got the lock 147-497 ms off the release (8 rounds; in 4 the waiter overtook the holder, which was itself in backoff); the 2 ms-poll lock 0-2 ms (8 of 8), exclusive, re-entrant, released on a raise.
findings.client_change_alone_regresses: ab.py, 6 rotating rounds at load 8.8-9.8, platform client vs this branch's client against the OLD VM code: old median 5535 [5171-6001], new 6532 [4890-10646], cold 3319 [3221-4714]. Attaching at once lands the request inside the boot's lock window sooner, and :global's backoff grows with every failed attempt. The client change must ship with the VM change (await-boot!).
findings.test_slower_in_the_warm_vm: Both paths take the SDK lease at the start of the isolated test run (retain_sdk_runtime! 730 ms cold, 754 ms warm), and every SDK namespace loaded after it re-derives the runtime inventory (sdk_runtime_inventory_uncached!): 107-115 ms per load in the cold VM, 174-214 ms in the warm one, which has ~20 more daemon namespaces loaded. reload.check took 171 ms cold, 387 ms warm. This is M4's retain_sdk_runtime! (priv/host/env.bl), not changed here.
findings.daemon_namespaces: Loaded through the one Loader.Server before the test starts, none of them by --cold: bl.realm-lifecycle 31-48, vm.client 35-62, vm.session 53-86, vm.net 20-32, vm.manager 34-42, vm.owner 162-212, proc.reg 131-175, proc.server 21-34, reload.declaration 49-64, reload.execution 25-34, vm.idle 60, vm.core 24-45, reload.generation 131-173 (vm.core/prepare-drain!), bl.daemon 32-42, vm.exec 28-62, vm.realm 27-49, vm.spec 25-42, vm.index 26-174, vm.registry 24-56 (ms, compile_sdk_source! per namespace). About 1 s of serialized loader work: with it on the critical path the warm first command cannot reach --cold.
findings.sampler: A 5 ms process sampler (sm1) perturbed the VM too much for timing (warm 6.7-7.0 s); it showed Loader.Server and file_server_2 as the busy processes, nothing else competing.

changes.tooling/drop (launcher.rs first_request,: The client that started the VM (or found a start in flight) sends the command as soon as the socket accepts it, retrying every 10 ms while nothing has read it, instead of a 200 ms readiness-hello poll and a second connection. A VM that exits unsuccessfully ends the wait at once, as before.
changes.priv/std/vm/session.bl (await-boot!): A command that arrives while its session is still in boot-realm-services! waits on a per-session atomics slot (2 ms poll, cleared in a finally) instead of racing the boot for its locks.
changes.priv/std/vm/manager.bl (trans), priv/std: The manager start and the realm lifecycle lock poll every 2 ms (`:global.set_lock` with 0 retries) instead of :global.trans's backoff; same lock ids, same nodes, re-entrant, released in a finally.
